## Søren Kierkegaard quote sources

8 passages attributed to Søren Kierkegaard in this archive, each with the locator that lets you find it in the work itself — and the one thing that most often goes wrong when people quote Kierkegaard.

[Quote source](https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source) / Søren Kierkegaard

How to cite this author, and what circulates under the name that is not theirs to give.

### Sourcing profile

Language of the works

Danish

Cited here from

The Sickness unto Death, The Concept of Anxiety, Either/Or, and the Journals (1843).

How to cite it

Name the pseudonym as well as Kierkegaard. The Sickness unto Death is signed by Anti-Climacus, The Concept of Anxiety by Vigilius Haufniensis, and Either/Or by two more, because the pseudonymity is part of the work rather than a pen name.

Where quotations of this author go wrong

Kierkegaard published his philosophical books under pseudonyms whose positions he did not simply hold, and he said so explicitly in “A First and Last Explanation,” which he signed with his own name. Quoting one of the pseudonyms as Kierkegaard's opinion is exactly the reading he wrote the explanation to prevent. The Journals are a separate corpus with their own numbering and dates.

### Frequently asked questions

#### Where can I check quotations attributed to Søren Kierkegaard?

Name the pseudonym as well as Kierkegaard. The Sickness unto Death is signed by Anti-Climacus, The Concept of Anxiety by Vigilius Haufniensis, and Either/Or by two more, because the pseudonymity is part of the work rather than a pen name. This archive cites Søren Kierkegaard from The Sickness unto Death, The Concept of Anxiety, Either/Or, and the Journals (1843). Every passage listed on this page carries that locator, so it can be found in any edition of the work.

#### What is the most common mistake when quoting Søren Kierkegaard?

Kierkegaard published his philosophical books under pseudonyms whose positions he did not simply hold, and he said so explicitly in “A First and Last Explanation,” which he signed with his own name. Quoting one of the pseudonyms as Kierkegaard's opinion is exactly the reading he wrote the explanation to prevent. The Journals are a separate corpus with their own numbering and dates.

#### What language did Søren Kierkegaard write in?

Danish. Any English sentence you read is a translation, so a complete source names the translator as well as the passage.
